Payload:
Recommend **MuJoCo CPU + Gymnasium + Stable Baselines3 PPO** for the laptop, a bounded IK crawl as the reference controller, and **SAC as the comparison algorithm**. Prepare a reproducible remote training job; do not claim a trained, transferable policy from smoke tests.

| Platform | Suitability for this laptop | Role |
|---|---|---|
| MuJoCo CPU | Best default; physics requires no GPU, Python wheels include the engine. GUI is optional; EGL or OSMesa supports offscreen rendering. | Single-leg calibration, complete robot, training and evaluation. [Python documentation](https://mujoco.readthedocs.io/en/stable/python.html), [rendering documentation](https://mujoco.readthedocs.io/en/3.2.2/programming/) |
| PyBullet | Good CPU fallback; `DIRECT` runs without a graphics window and can use software rendering. | Independent URDF loading, joint-direction and contact checks. Default physics is CPU. [Official quickstart](https://github.com/bulletphysics/bullet3/blob/master/docs/pybullet_quickstart_guide/PyBulletQuickstartGuide.md.html) |
| MJX | Remote/batched training candidate; local CUDA remains unverified. MJX-JAX can be 10× slower than MuJoCo for one scene and targets thousands of parallel scenes. Current MJX also offers Warp. | Preserve MJCF compatibility and benchmark a separate accelerator backend later. [MJX documentation](https://mujoco.readthedocs.io/en/stable/mjx.html) |
| Genesis | Optional GPU experiment after driver verification; CPU backend also exists. Its official Go2 PPO example is deliberately minimal. | Secondary batched training candidate, starting with a small environment count. No GTX1650 speed estimate is justified without measurements. [Installation](https://genesis-world.readthedocs.io/en/latest/user_guide/overview/installation.html), [locomotion example](https://genesis-world.readthedocs.io/en/v1.4.0/user_guide/policy_training/examples/locomotion.html) |
| Isaac Sim / standard Isaac Lab | Unsuitable locally: current Isaac Sim minimum lists 32 GB RAM, RTX4080, 16 GB VRAM; GPUs without RT cores are unsupported. | Optional remote RTX workstation backend. Isaac Lab adds training memory requirements. [Isaac Sim requirements](https://docs.isaacsim.omniverse.nvidia.com/latest/installation/requirements.html), [Isaac Lab installation](https://isaac-sim.github.io/IsaacLab/develop/source/setup/installation/index.html) |
| Gazebo Sim | Available headless; useful if ROS integration becomes important. Adds unnecessary integration work for the initial learning pipeline. | Later firmware/ROS interface checks. [Official server-only instructions](https://github.com/gazebosim/docs/blob/master/common/get_started.md), [headless rendering](https://gazebosim.org/api/sim/7/headless_rendering.html) |

PPO with a small MLP should initially run on CPU: SB3 explicitly recommends CPU and process-based environments for this configuration. Benchmark 1, 2 and 4 workers instead of assuming more workers improve throughput. SAC supplies an off-policy continuous-control comparison, but a short run only proves the training pipeline executes. [PPO documentation](https://stable-baselines3.readthedocs.io/en/master/modules/ppo.html), [SAC documentation](https://stable-baselines3.readthedocs.io/en/master/modules/sac.html), [RL guidance](https://stable-baselines3.readthedocs.io/en/master/guide/rl_tips.html)

Important actuator evidence: **STS3215 identifies multiple variants.** FEETECH distinguishes a 7.4 V C001 and a 12 V C018. For **C018 at 12 V**, the manufacturer specifies 55±1 g, 0.222 s/60° no-load speed, 30 kg·cm peak stall torque, **10 kg·cm rated torque**, 2.7 A stall current and half-duplex serial communication up to 1 Mbps. These convert to approximately 4.72 rad/s, 2.94 N·m peak and 0.981 N·m rated torque. The variant and supply must therefore be explicit configuration choices. Peak stall torque must never become an unlimited sustainable simulation torque. [Variant catalogue](https://www.feetechrc.com/products.html?keyword=STS3215), [C018 manufacturer specifications](https://www.feetechrc.com/525603.html)

Recommended position-servo approximation: delayed, quantized and slew-limited position targets; bounded PD torque; speed-dependent torque envelope; motor friction/deadband; configuration for battery voltage and thermal/current derating. Encoder quantization is approximately `2π/4096`. PD gains, backlash, loaded speed, latency and thermal parameters remain **estimated until single-leg identification**. Manufacturer specs do not provide a fully identified servo model. MuJoCo provides actuator/joint force bounds, but dynamics must still be calibrated. [MuJoCo force limits](https://mujoco.readthedocs.io/en/stable/XMLreference.html#body-joint-actuatorfrcrange)

Suggested implementation/evaluation structure:

1. Single fixed-body leg: verify axes, limits, FK/IK and reachable workspace; run step and sine tracking under multiple loads.
2. Whole robot: verify mass/inertia validity, static standing, self-collision, foot clearance and bounded IK crawl.
3. Command-conditioned policy for `(vx, vy, yaw_rate)`, with forward/backward/left/right and stop evaluations. Prefer bounded residual joint/foot offsets around IK, initially.
4. Actor observations only from available hardware: IMU-derived orientation/angular rate, measured joint position/velocity, command, previous action and optional history. Perfect world velocity and exact foot contact belong to reward/evaluation or a privileged critic unless an equivalent real estimator/sensor exists.
5. Randomize plausible uncertainty: link masses with consistent inertia scaling, body COM, friction, motor strength/gains, command delay, sensor noise, voltage and pushes. Phone payload must change mass, COM **and inertia**, including absent/present and placement configurations.
6. Gradually introduce low-friction floors, gentle slopes and modest heightfields. A friction change alone does not emulate carpet deformation, sand, mud or loose gravel.
7. Held-out evaluation across commands, surfaces, payloads and seeds; report fall rate, velocity error, yaw drift, clearance, saturation and episode survival, rather than reward alone.

Accurate actuators and latency matter more than blindly broad randomization: primary quadruped work found randomization could not compensate for severe actuator mismatch, while later ablations found unnecessary randomization can make policies conservative. Use parameter sweeps to identify relevant uncertainty. [Tan et al., sim-to-real quadruped locomotion](https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.10332), [Dynamics Randomization Revisited](https://arxiv.org/abs/2011.02404)

**Measured-versus-estimated boundary:** local GPU presence does not establish usable CUDA; missing `nvidia-smi` is not proof that the card cannot compute. Record driver availability, framework device detection, peak memory and actual rollout throughput before enabling GPU presets. JAX currently requires Linux driver ≥525 for CUDA12 or ≥580 for CUDA13; verify compatibility before installing. [JAX installation requirements](https://docs.jax.dev/en/latest/installation.html)

A smoke-trained checkpoint, synthetic CAD masses and approximate servo dynamics can be delivered as a working simulation pipeline. Real-world gait reliability remains unverified until dimensions, masses, joint zeros, servo response and sensor timing are measured, followed by supported low-speed hardware tests.

Completed the model/export layer in `outputs/mist-robot/locomotion`:

- `model.py`, `config.json`, `kinematics.py`
- Fixed test-leg and floating quadruped URDFs with CAD visuals
- `models/model_report.json` with source hashes, inertials and assumptions

The quadruped removes the 69.089 g bench fixture using mesh-derived inertia subtraction. Nominal mass is **2.648187 kg with phone**, **2.493187 kg without**. Mounts match the main-hub CAD: 75 mm radius, 38 mm yaw height, ±45°/±135° orientations.

The phone uses the source upright landscape pose, with 55 g pan-servo and 6 g horn allowances. Mount compatibility and unmeasured harness/cradle masses remain explicit assumptions.

Model export takes about **0.249 s cold**, **0.0123 s cached**. Config is stable and matches the requested actuator/rate settings.

Payload:
Implemented:

- `locomotion/train.py`: PPO/SAC, seeded vector environments, fixed validation suite, checkpoints, SAC replay buffers, resume, metrics, strict CUDA checks, effective model parameters and source-change guard.
- `locomotion/scripts/benchmark.py`, `train_smoke.sh`, `run_job.py`, `run_training.sh`.
- `locomotion/training_queue.json`: six portable jobs, prepared only.
- `locomotion/RESEARCH.md`: primary sources, simulator comparison, motor limitations and integration-convergence evidence.

Trainer syntax, queue dry-run, unavailable-CUDA rejection, provenance guard and actual PPO/SAC resumption passed. **No training jobs are running.** Earlier checkpoints and benchmarks were retired under `work/` after geometry, frame and integration corrections. There is no current qualified policy.

After the gait/environment/remote integration is frozen, run from the workspace:

```bash
work/py311/bin/python outputs/mist-robot/locomotion/scripts/benchmark.py --steps 2000 --warmup 100

MIST_PYTHON="$PWD/work/py311/bin/python" \
bash outputs/mist-robot/locomotion/scripts/train_smoke.sh \
outputs/mist-robot/locomotion/runs/smoke
```

Then run each algorithm with:

```bash
work/py311/bin/python outputs/mist-robot/locomotion/train.py \
  --algo ppo --terrain mixed --timesteps 51200 --n-envs 4 \
  --seed 42 --device cpu \
  --eval-terrains flat low_friction slope rough \
  --eval-payloads '[0,0.155]' --eval-episodes 1 \
  --eval-max-steps 960 --eval-freq 25000 --checkpoint-freq 25000 \
  --output outputs/mist-robot/locomotion/runs/ppo_51200
```

Repeat with `--algo sac` and `runs/sac_51200`. **51,200 steps gives matched actual budgets** because PPO’s 2,048-step rollout rounds 50,000 upward.

Pending: final benchmark/smoke, matched longer runs, untouched evaluation matrix, final resume checks, and updated hardware research for the reported Ultra 9 / 64 GB / RTX4080 mobile computer. Research currently identifies its hardware comparison as applying to the initially inspected laptop.

Payload:
Integrated and froze `gait.py`.

- Added `position_targets()` with scheduled support loads and source-based gravity compensation.
- Uses nominal CAD masses and gains plus known phone mass; no simulator contacts or hidden motor parameters.
- Bounds position bias to ±0.12 rad and source joint limits.
- **5 tests passed**, including four directions at 1000 Hz with phone and 0.588 Nm limit, no falls or IK rejections.

Diagnostics saved under `locomotion/runs/diagnostics`. Exact 1000 Hz experiments achieved approximately **0.094–0.098 m in all four directions over 12 seconds**.

Also confirmed the two critical simulation fixes: recover the body frame from PyBullet’s inertial frame, and use approximately 1000 Hz physics to avoid unstable discrete motor damping.
